headings.title: Introduction to the Misoprostol-Only Regimen
headings.content: The **misoprostol-only regimen** is a medical method used for pregnancy termination and the management of early pregnancy loss. Because of its stability at room temperature and broad availability, it serves a vital role in resource-constrained settings across sub-Saharan Africa. Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin E1 analogue originally developed to prevent NSAID-induced gastric ulcers. Its uterotonic properties make it an effective, non-invasive alternative to surgical evacuation when combined with appropriate clinical protocols.

headings.title: Mechanism of Action and Pharmacology
headings.content: Pharmacologically, misoprostol acts directly on myometrial cells to induce strong, rhythmic uterine contractions. It binds to prostaglandin E receptors, leading to intracellular calcium influx and muscle shortening. Simultaneously, it promotes cervical ripening by modifying collagen networks and increasing water content in the stroma. Peak plasma concentrations occur fastest via the sublingual route, followed by buccal, vaginal, and oral administration.

headings.title: Clinical Indications and Eligibility
headings.content:
- **First-trimester termination**: Used for elective or therapeutic termination of pregnancies up to a specific gestational age limit.
- **Incomplete abortion**: Promotes the expulsion of retained products of conception following a spontaneous miscarriage.
- **Missed abortion**: Facilitates the clearance of non-viable embryonic or fetal tissue from the uterine cavity.
- **Ectopic pregnancy exclusion**: Must be ruled out via clinical exam or ultrasound before administration, as misoprostol is ineffective and unsafe for extra-uterine implants.

headings.title: Standard Dosage and Administration Routes
headings.content: Dosage protocols depend strictly on the gestational age and clinical indication. For first-trimester termination, repeated doses of 800 mcg vaginally, buccally, or sublingually are common. Buccal and sublingual routes require holding tablets in place for a specified duration before swallowing remnants. Vaginal administration requires adequate moisture and a resting client position to ensure optimal tablet dissolution and absorption.

headings.title: Pre-Procedure Assessment and Counseling
headings.content: Before dispensing medication, nurses must confirm gestational age, establish dating, and check for contraindications such as known prostaglandin allergy or severe hepatic impairment. Counseling involves setting realistic expectations: bleeding will be heavier than a normal menstrual period, and cramping will intensify as the process peaks. Clients must understand when the expected effects cross the line into dangerous complications requiring immediate hospital return.

headings.title: Expected Side Effects and Normal Process
headings.content: Common systemic side effects of misoprostol include transient chills, low-grade fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. These symptoms stem from the systemic action of prostaglandins on smooth muscle and the thermoregulatory center. They typically resolve within hours without specific intervention. Uterine cramping and heavy bleeding with clots are the desired pharmacological effects, signaling that the treatment is progressing normally.

headings.title: Complications and Warning Signs
headings.content: Although generally safe, the regimen carries risks that require vigilant monitoring. Excessive hemorrhage—defined as soaking through two large sanitary pads per hour for two consecutive hours—indicates potential incomplete abortion or atony. Signs of pelvic infection, such as persistent foul-smelling discharge, severe pelvic pain not relieved by analgesics, or prolonged fever beyond 24 hours, warrant urgent clinical evaluation and possible antibiotic therapy.

headings.title: Post-Abortion Follow-Up and Contraception
headings.content: Routine follow-up ensures complete abortion and assesses the client's physical recovery. Clinicians verify that bleeding has tapered and systemic symptoms have resolved. Because fertility returns almost immediately—often within two weeks of abortion—contraceptive counseling and initiation must occur before the client leaves the facility. Most methods, including oral contraceptive pills, injectables, implants, and intrauterine devices, can be started on the same day the misoprostol regimen is administered.
